source.title_on_document: The Dynamics of Collective Creativity in Human-AI Hybrid Societies

paper_design_summary: UK native-English Prolific participants selected and elaborated neighboring stories in human-only or hybrid human-AI networks, alongside an AI-only network benchmark; each person contributed once (PDF p. 3, Method). The paper explicitly randomizes node location but does not explicitly describe allocation of people between human-only and hybrid network conditions (PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity). A separate validation study supplied human creativity ratings, and collective diversity was computed from TF-IDF cosine similarities among stories within iteration groups; hybrid-network summaries include both human and AI stories (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity and Results).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Node location was explicitly randomly assigned to participants. Assignment of humans to human-only versus human-AI network composition, the contrast determining generative-AI exposure, was not explicitly described.
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one location (node) in the network and only contributed once to the experiment.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 3, Method, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity, first paragraph and condition descriptions

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: All nodes were occupied by human participants; participants selected and modified neighboring human stories. Reported condition N=625 (PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity).

arms.name: AI-only
arms.description: All nodes were simulated using GPT-4o. The reported 625 calls to the OpenAI API are not a people count (PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity).

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: Hybrid network described as 50% human participants and 50% GPT-4o agents, with human N=254. Humans were not informed that stories could be AI-generated (PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity).

participants.who: Prolific participants recruited from the UK who identified English as their native language. The reported storytelling sample is 879 people, with condition Ns of 625 human-only and 254 human-AI. The total is described as recruited; no separate post-exclusion count is given. The separate validation raters are not included in this storytelling count.
participants.quote: In total, we recruited 879 human participants and conducted 996 calls to GPT-4o (Hurst et al., 2024), using the version released on September 3, 2024.
participants.locator: PDF p. 3, Method, Participants and Network Experiments on Collective Creativity; PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity (separate rater sample)

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4o; version released on September 3, 2024, as stated in the paper (PDF p. 3, Participants)
ai_tool.how_used: AI agents selected and generated stories within the network; people in the hybrid condition could select and elaborate neighboring stories without being told whether their source was AI. This was exposure through network stories, rather than a participant-operated chat interface (PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity; PDF p. 6, Limitations and conclusion).

task.description: Select and creatively elaborate a neighboring story in a 5×5 network. All networks began with the same story about John, a missing key, and his cat; stories were transmitted over 25 iterations, with each human contributing once (PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity).

outcomes.name: Human-rated creativity of stories on a 5-point scale
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Human-AI: M = 2.327, SD = 1.159, 95% CI: [2.184, 2.576]; Human-only: M = 2.482, SD = 1.026, 95% CI: [2.389, 2.576]. The text describes these conditions as similar but prints p < .001 after this comparison; the wording, p-value, and intervals are preserved without correction. The hybrid result is for the network story pool, not a separately reported human-authored subset.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity; Results, Creativity and Diversity, first paragraph (continues from left to right column); Figure 2A

contrasts.reported: Separate first-to-last creativity changes: GPT/AI-only M = 0.464, SD = 0.154, p < 0.001; Human-AI M = 0.264, SD = 0.175, p < 0.001; Human-only M = −0.133, SD = 0.067, p = 1.000. These are separate within-condition changes across network iterations, not a reported between-condition effect or difference in changes. The Human-AI estimate combines human and AI stories. Each human contributed once, so these are not repeated measurements of the same creative-task participants.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 4, Results: Creativity and Diversity, first paragraph continued in the right column; Figure 2C and caption (first-to-last gain). PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity (one contribution per human).

outcomes.name: Collective story diversity: inverse mean pairwise cosine similarity of TF-IDF vectors
outcomes.question: across_people

contrasts.reported: Human-AI: M = 0.860, SD = 0.043, 95% CI: [0.806, 0.913]; Human-only: M = 0.823, SD = 0.019, 95% CI: [0.800, 0.900]. These are reported network-condition summaries of diversity within iteration groups; no numerical test of this between-condition difference is supplied. The hybrid pool includes human and AI stories. Intervals are recorded exactly as printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity, diversity paragraph; Results, Creativity and Diversity, paragraph beginning Next, we looked; Figure 2B

diversity_detail.metric: Diversity is described as the inverse of the mean pairwise cosine similarity of TF-IDF story vectors, with lower similarity indicating greater diversity. No explicit algebraic transformation is given (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: TF-IDF vectorization; no learned embedding model is specified for this diversity measure (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity).
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of stories within each network condition and predefined iteration group. Figure 2 groups the 25 iterations into five sets of five. Human-AI groups contain both human and AI stories (PDF p. 3, condition definitions; PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity and Figure 2 caption).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Figure 2 describes error bars as one standard deviation computed across participants. The Results report SDs and 95% confidence intervals, but do not explain how the intervals were constructed. No numerical test of the Human-AI versus Human-only diversity-level difference is supplied (PDF p. 4, Figure 2 caption and Results: Creativity and Diversity).
diversity_detail.notes: Hybrid summaries do not isolate human-authored stories. The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings belong to the separate UMAP visualization, not the TF-IDF diversity measure (PDF pp. 3-4, condition definitions and Measures of Creativity; PDF pp. 4-5, Semantic Analysis of Stories).

outcomes.name: Change in collective story diversity across network iterations (TF-IDF cosine measure)
outcomes.question: across_people

contrasts.reported: Human-AI diversity gain: M = 0.098, SD = 0.039, 95% CI: [0.064, 0.131]; AI-only diversity change: M = −0.034, SD = 0.17, 95% CI: [-0.047, -0.021]. The paper states that Human-AI reached the highest diversity in the final iterations. These are separate within-condition changes, not a reported difference-in-changes estimate; the AI-only SD is transcribed as 0.17. This compares a mixed human/AI story pool with an entirely AI-generated pool.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 4, Results, Creativity and Diversity, paragraph beginning However, the evolution; Figure 2D and caption

diversity_detail.metric: Diversity is described as the inverse of the mean pairwise cosine similarity of TF-IDF story vectors, with lower similarity indicating greater diversity. No explicit algebraic transformation is given (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: TF-IDF vectorization; no learned embedding model is specified for this diversity measure (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity).
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of stories within each network condition and predefined iteration group. Figure 2 groups the 25 iterations into five sets of five. Human-AI groups contain both human and AI stories (PDF p. 3, condition definitions; PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity and Figure 2 caption). For the change outcome, Figure 2D and its caption describe gain from the first iteration to the last (PDF p. 4).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Figure 2 describes error bars as one standard deviation computed across participants. The Results report SDs and 95% confidence intervals for the separate within-condition changes, but do not explain how the intervals were constructed. No between-condition difference in changes or numerical test of that difference is supplied (PDF p. 4, Figure 2 caption and Results: Creativity and Diversity).
diversity_detail.notes: Hybrid summaries do not isolate human-authored stories. The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings belong to the separate UMAP visualization, not the TF-IDF diversity measure (PDF pp. 3-4, condition definitions and Measures of Creativity; PDF pp. 4-5, Semantic Analysis of Stories).

studies.label: Validation study: independent human creativity ratings for S1

assignment.what_was_assigned: Raters received randomized selections of stories from all network conditions and iterations. The text describes random selection of rating stimuli, not random assignment of people to generative-AI assistance.
assignment.quote: Each participant was presented with a randomized selection of stories from all experimental conditions and iterations and asked to rate their creativity on a 5-point scale, ranging from 1 (not creative at all) to 5 (extremely creative).
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity, first paragraph

arms.name: Independent validation raters
arms.description: One separate group evaluated stories sampled across all experimental conditions and iterations, without being informed whether stories were human- or AI-generated (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity).

participants.who: Separate group of human creativity raters. The Methods text describes 100 human participants (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity), but Figure 1C labels the evaluation sample N=94 human (PDF p. 2). The paper does not reconcile these counts or identify recruitment versus exclusions, so the analyzed count is unconfirmed. Recruitment source and demographics are not specified separately for this validation sample. These raters provide outcome ratings for S1 and are not additional creative-task participants for eligibility.
participants.quote: To assess the quality of creations across conditions and iterations, we conducted a validation study with a separate group of 100 human participants.
participants.locator: PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity, first paragraph (100 human participants); PDF p. 2, Figure 1C, green label beneath the rating interface (N=94 human; visually verified from a PDF rendering in memory)

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4o generated some of the stories being rated; no generative-AI tool was provided to raters.
ai_tool.how_used: AI-generated stories were rating stimuli, with their origin undisclosed. The ratings are recorded as the creativity outcome of S1, without duplicating that outcome here (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity).

task.description: Each rater evaluated 20 stories for creativity on a 5-point scale from 1 (not creative at all) to 5 (extremely creative); this was a rating task, not production of creative output (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity).

eligibility.reason: Core remains unclear. Random assignment is stated for network node location, but allocation between human-only and human-AI network compositions is not described; no non-random allocation mechanism is stated either (PDF p. 3, Network Experiments on Collective Creativity). Criterion 2 is also unclear: 879 is explicitly a recruited storytelling count, and 625 human-only and 254 human-AI are reported condition Ns, without confirmed post-exclusion analysis counts (PDF p. 3, Participants and condition descriptions; PDF p. 2, Figure 1B). This is not evidence that fewer than 50 people were analyzed. Human creativity ratings and TF-IDF diversity scores assess produced stories, satisfying criterion 3 (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity and Results). The explicit AI-only versus human-only output benchmark qualifies as ai_vs_human context; the hybrid assistance comparison remains an unconfirmed design rather than a confirmed RCT or non-random comparison (PDF pp. 3-4, condition definitions and Creativity and Diversity; codebook sections 3-4). Hybrid summaries combine human and AI stories and do not establish a separate human-authored-output effect. The validation raters are not creative-task participants; their count conflicts between 100 in the methods and 94 in Figure 1C (PDF p. 4, Measures of Creativity; PDF p. 2, Figure 1C).

one_line_finding: Hybrid-network diversity increased (M = 0.098) while AI-only diversity decreased (M = −0.034), but random allocation to network composition is not explicit (PDF p. 4, Results and Figure 2D; PDF p. 3, Method).
